solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Prime Minister receives everyone — everyone in Westminster thoroughfare

indicators.note: the Prime Minister's abbreviation takes the next piece inside it, as a host receives a guest

parts.note: everyone means all
again, everyone means all

explanation.surface: The PM welcomes all comers on a famous London street.
explanation.walkthrough: PALL MALL is a street in Westminster, London, running from Trafalgar Square towards St James's Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: A named street in the City of Westminster, home to many gentlemen's clubs.

clue.text: Agile medic goes into river

indicators.note: the medic's letters are placed within the river's name

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, stands for a doctor

explanation.surface: A sprightly doctor plunges into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: both describe someone quick and light in movement.

clue.text: Illegal occupier of property is more stocky

definitions.meaning: someone who lives in a building without any right to it
comparative of an adjective meaning short and thickset

explanation.surface: The person living unlawfully in the house is also rather thickset.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the noun for an unlawful resident; the other is the comparative of squat, meaning short and broad.

clue.text: Son given very warm drink

parts.note: very warm means hot

explanation.surface: A boy is handed a steaming beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A small measure of spirits, downed in one, is a common name for a drink.

clue.text: Insufficiently sliced steak

definitions.meaning: read as two words, not chopped enough
a cut of beef from the underside of the sirloin

explanation.surface: A cook complains that the beef has not been carved thinly enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, it means not cut enough; whole, it names the tenderloin cut of beef.

clue.text: Temporary accommodation receiving a new renter

indicators.note: the shelter takes the following letters into its middle

parts.note: a tent is a shelter put up for a short time

explanation.surface: A campsite welcomes someone fresh who is paying rent.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: someone who pays to occupy property owned by a landlord.

clue.text: Nobleman covered in pearls

indicators.note: the answer sits wrapped inside the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: An aristocrat dripping with jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A British peer ranking above a viscount and below a marquess.

clue.text: Some Europeans hurry round Northern Ireland

indicators.note: the word for hurry goes around the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: to hurry is to dash

explanation.surface: Travellers rush about the province of Ulster.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Denmark are a group of Europeans.

clue.text: Plain gold coin used in Kuwait and Yemeni capital

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
the dinar is the currency of Kuwait

indicators.note: the capital, or opening letter, of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A simple golden coin circulating in two Arabian states.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: plain and everyday both describe something unremarkable.

clue.text: Turning thin wood mostly is a piece of cake

indicators.note: the shortened wood is turned round, read from end to start
most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: balsa is a very light wood, sold in thin sheets for models

explanation.surface: Woodworking with thin sheets is supposedly easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts BALSA to BALS, and 'Turning' reverses that. 'piece of cake' looks like 'easy', but here it is a literal thick slice.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick flat portion, as of fruit cake, is a common name for a hefty helping.

clue.text: Race for all to see in Navy

indicators.note: the letter for general audiences sits inside the abbreviation for the navy

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A sailing contest held in full public view.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British cinema rating for a film anyone may watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a sprint or jog against others, as in a fun run.

clue.text: A joke drowned by microphone, briefly? Great!

indicators.note: the joke is swallowed up inside the short form of microphone

parts.note: mic is the short form of microphone
a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: A comic's punchline is lost under the noise from the microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: both words mean grand, splendid, impressive in scale.

clue.text: Important people drink endlessly, having money

indicators.note: the word for drink loses its final letter

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily
brass is British slang for money

explanation.surface: Bigwigs keep drinking, since they can afford it.
explanation.walkthrough: BRASS is informal northern English for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the senior officers or leaders of an organisation.

clue.text: Sign to approve credit

definitions.meaning: the check mark written beside something correct
informal British for buying now and paying later

explanation.surface: A mark that authorises a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the check mark used to show approval; the other is British slang for deferred payment.

clue.text: Agnostic at sea, cruising

indicators.note: confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A non-believer on an ocean voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: both describe moving along easily with little effort.

clue.text: Still sick, accepting these?

indicators.note: the two words take the answer into themselves, holding it within

explanation.surface: A patient remains unwell, having to put up with troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the answer is held within 'Still sick', and a sick person is one who accepts these.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailments and misfortunes are what a person who is still unwell has to endure.

clue.text: Arrange to leave

definitions.meaning: to lay out or display in order

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to lay things out in order and to begin a journey.

clue.text: Father's prenatal exercising

indicators.note: putting the letters through their paces, working them into a new order

explanation.surface: A dad attends antenatal workout classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father's' is possessive, matching the adjective: of or belonging to a father.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to a father, as in fatherly care.

clue.text: Refuse to admit about a hundred in plane

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the hundred goes inside the aircraft

parts.note: a jet is a plane
C is the Roman numeral for one hundred

explanation.surface: An airline turns away a hundred passengers on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse to admit' looks like a denial of guilt but means turning someone away.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn away an applicant or visitor is to decline them entry.

clue.text: English bishops decline

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: The Church of England's senior clergy are in decline.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: as a verb, to fade away or diminish, like a tide going out.

clue.text: Tortilla and steak cook regularly supplied

indicators.note: every other letter of the two words is taken, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A recipe: steak cooked and served in a wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A folded corn tortilla with a filling is the Mexican dish named here.

clue.text: Sparkling wine in the region of Virginia

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means roughly or about
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Fizz produced somewhere near Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish sparkling wine made by the traditional method, like champagne.

clue.text: Just organised projects

indicators.note: sorted into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has simply got their schemes in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'projects' looks like a noun for schemes but is the verb meaning sticks out.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: as a verb, both mean to stick out or protrude.

clue.text: View old liner finally going through a canal in S America

indicators.note: the old letter and the liner's end pass into the middle of the canal's name

parts.note: the Panama Canal links the Atlantic and Pacific

indicators.note: the last letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: An old ocean liner sails through the Panama Canal.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a wide, sweeping outlook over a landscape.

clue.text: Empty metal container covered by tax

indicators.note: the container sits inside the tax, which wraps around it

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, a UK sales tax
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A tin with nothing in it still gets taxed.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: unoccupied or holding nothing.

clue.text: A. N .Other's drunk lots of water

indicators.note: the letters reel about like a drunkard, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Anonymous has been knocking back huge quantities of water.
explanation.walkthrough: A. N. Other is the British placeholder name for an unnamed person, as on a team sheet; the apostrophe S joins the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sea between Britain and mainland Europe is a great body of water.
